title: Drift-detector suppressor and safe rollforward for orphaned Helm hooks
creator: Diego Morales
description: Several on-prem customer upgrades failed when Helm post-upgrade hooks produced long-running resources (jobs/cronjobs) that became orphaned after a partial Helm release failure. The operator's drift detector subsequently suppressed reconciliation attempts for those resources because they looked like operator-applied objects, leaving the cluster in a degraded state and blocking subsequent upgrades. This ticket implements a conservative suppressor mitigation for the drift detector plus a safe rollforward path that garbage-collects known orphaned Helm hooks and unsticks affected CRs without forcing a full rollback.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Install chart v1.4.2 on a constrained on-prem cluster where node pressure causes pod evictions mid-upgrade
2) Trigger upgrade to chart v1.4.3 where templates add a post-upgrade Hook that creates a Job+ConfigMap; the hook is annotated helm.sh/hook=post-upgrade
3) Simulate an interrupted Helm release (helm upgrade --atomic on flaky control-plane) so the release record is in a transient failed state

4) Observe Job/ConfigMap remain running/created but have no owner reference tying them to a stable release and the operator's drift detector marks them as user-managed and suppresses reconciles for their associated CRs
5) Subsequent upgrade attempts fail preflight because preflight sees leftover hook artifacts and blocks with a 'stale-hook-detected' error
root_cause: Helm post-upgrade hooks created resources whose lifecycle was not fully reconciled when an upgrade aborted. Operator drift detector heuristics classified those resources as externally-managed and suppressed further reconciles. The combination of (a) Helm upgrade/atomic behavior, (b) unreliable preflight cleanup when upgrades abort, and (c) overly-broad suppression rules allowed orphaned hook artifacts to persist and block future upgrades.
mitigation: Implement a two-part mitigation: (A) a temporary drift-detector suppressor: when the operator detects a failed/in-flight Helm release for the same release name/namespace, reduce the suppression window and raise the confidence threshold to allow a short reconciliation attempt for resources annotated with helm.sh/hook; (B) safe rollforward: a guarded garbage-collection flow that targets only well-known hook resource kinds (Job, CronJob, ConfigMap) with matching helm hook annotations and a short TTL annotation (redwood/orphan-check=true). This flow will take a snapshot, attempt a deterministic cleanup, and run lightweight validation checks to avoid deleting customer-managed resources.
hotfix_pr: https://github.com/redwood-inference/operator/pull/2497 - drift-detector: allow tentative reconcile for helm hooks (WIP)
comments: 2026-03-10 - Diego Morales: Initial investigation found 6 customer clusters with the same pattern. Reproduced locally with a minikube scenario where the post-upgrade job never completed and Helm left the release in a FAILED state.

2026-03-11 - Asha Patel: Scoped fast-path hotfix: allow operator to detect helm.sh/hook annotations and attempt a single reconcile even if drift detector would otherwise suppress. Drafted PR with unit tests; running cluster smoke tests now.

2026-03-11 - SRE (review): Please ensure GC flow requires both (a) release appears failed for >5m and (b) resource has redwood/orphan-check=true annotation before deletion. Avoid deleting customer-created resources.

2026-03-12 - Asha Patel: Added e2e that simulates interrupted upgrade and verifies post-upgrade hook-cleaner removes only annotated hook ConfigMaps/Jobs. Deployed hotfix to canary onprem customer (canary-2) — initial verification shows preflight no longer blocks subsequent upgrade attempts.

2026-03-12 - PM (Olivia Chen): Notifying support and drafting customer communication. We will include a step-by-step rollback and recommended preflight checks for customers planning upgrades in the next 72 hours.
next_steps: Merge hotfix PRs after SRE signoff and deploy to onprem canary fleet (target 2026-03-13)
Monitor upgrade success rate and relevant Grafana panels for 48 hours; escalate if regressions appear
Add longer-term operator change: add helm release lock handshake annotation and include a Helm hook liveness probe in chart templates (follow-up ticket)
Document safe rollback/restore steps for customers and add pre-upgrade lint that flags potential long-running hooks
